instruction.text: This is the Lake District. Select the lake in the distance to learn more.

feedback.end: Edgar has brought you here to do some fieldwork! He wants to prove that it is colder at the summit of a mountain than at the bottom.

instruction.text: First, we need to find somewhere to park. Find the car park on the map.

feedback.end: Well Done! Car parks are always marked with this P symbol. This is where we will set off from.

instruction.text: Edgar thinks we should go up Grange Head to measure the temperature at the summit. In which direction do we need to go?
Which symbol on the map shows that Grange Head is a mountain?

feedback.end: Great work! Understanding our map is very important when we go walking, otherwise we might get lost!

instruction.text: Before we start walking, we need to check the temperature! What does the thermometer say the temperature is?.

feedback.correct: Good work! Now let’s start walking.

instruction.text: You reach a fork in the path. Select the signpost you should follow for Grange Head.

feedback.correct: Great! Signposts tell us the direction and distance to different landmarks. In the UK, distances are usually given in miles.

instruction.text: Finally, we’ve reached the summit of Grange Head! What is the temperature at the summit?

feedback.correct: Great! It is definitely colder up here - there’s even snow!

instruction.text: Which statement about your field trip is true?

b.sound: We proved that the temperature is colder at the summit of mountains.
We proved that the temperature is the same at the summit and the base of mountains.
